findings.title: Out-of-scope catch-all leaves edge cases undefined
findings.problem: The out-of-scope list ends in an open 'anything else', so the role boundary depends on the model's judgment rather than an explicit abstention path in the system prompt.
findings.proof: Out of scope: buying, paying, orders, accounts, discounts, messages, files, pictures; health, legal or money advice; anything else.
findings.fix: Replace 'anything else' with an explicit rule that out-of-scope requests receive the off_topic fixed reply and at most one in-scope alternative.

findings.title: No catalog recall or safety-notice check
findings.problem: The recall check is specified only for web-sourced products, and nothing requires checking recall or safety notices for catalog products shown in the table, which is missing from the system prompt's Enforced-by-code and Claims sections.
findings.fix: Add a rule to the Claims section that every product shown, catalog or web, is checked for recall or safety notices before it is recommended.

findings.title: Silent 25% budget loosening conflicts with the hard-limit rule
findings.problem: The system prompt treats the budget as a hard limit that stays fixed when the shopper invites going over it, but the catalog tool raises the budget by 25% during loosening, so the two rules clash unless the reply reports the loosened price.
findings.proof: claims, materials, products with no stated age, brand, category, the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: Either state in the system prompt that a 25% raise is reported as a miss against the budget, or set the price_max loosening to off for budget-constrained searches.

findings.title: Tool-result fence for the shopper's own message is not declared
findings.problem: The fenced inputs list covers tool results, earlier turns and products on screen, but the shopper's raw transcript passed to the Router and Planner has no declared data fence, so it is not marked as data in the prompts.
findings.fix: Add the shopper's transcript to the declared fence list (for example <shopper_message>) and state in the Router and Planner prompts that its contents are data, not instructions.

findings.title: Grounding index that the knowledge file describes is not supplied
findings.problem: The knowledge file calls the brand, category, material and claim lists 'complete indexes', but none of these lists is in the supplied corpus, so the agent cannot check unmatched_filters or validate claims before using them.
findings.fix: Ship the brand, category, material and listing-claim indexes as a knowledge file, or remove the claim that they are complete.

findings.title: Router paragraph is convoluted and repeats the planner's job
findings.problem: The Router stage carries a long multi-clause re-reading rule that restates the Planner's routing logic, costing tokens on every turn.
findings.proof: A message it would answer with fixed sentences alone is read once more by a model, for a buried product request and nothing else;
findings.fix: Shorten the rule to one sentence stating that a message with a buried product request gets a second routing pass, and remove the restated reply-ordering detail.

findings.title: Catalog size and snapshot date repeated across tool schema and knowledge file
findings.problem: The catalog's dataset name, size and snapshot date appear in the rag.search description and again in the knowledge file, so the same facts are paid for twice.
findings.proof: Amazon Product Dataset 2020; 9,740 products; listings and prices are a January 2020 snapshot
findings.fix: Keep the catalog facts in one place (the knowledge file) and reduce the tool description to a pointer.

findings.title: Loosening order duplicated between tool description and system prompt
findings.problem: The full loosening sequence is spelled out in the rag.search description while the system prompt separately restates which filters the tool may loosen, creating duplicate guidance.
findings.proof: Loosening: when fewer products than `top_k` meet every filter, filters are loosened in this order until enough are found
findings.fix: Keep the full loosening order in the schema only and have the system prompt refer to it in one short clause.

findings.title: Rule-check paragraph restates the Claims and Policy sections
findings.problem: The rule-checks paragraph repeats claim, rating and price rules already stated in the Claims section of the safety policy, adding redundant prompt tokens.
findings.proof: Rule checks on a draft. A dollar amount, rating or stock status must be a source's own, of a product the answer is about;
findings.fix: Replace the rule-check paragraph with a single reference to the Claims section for the claim rules and keep only the code-only checks.

findings.title: Tool schema descriptions are long for a two-tool surface
findings.problem: The rag.search description is long and mixes usage guidance, loosening logic and dataset facts, which makes the schema harder to scan and costs tokens on every call.
findings.proof: Not for a current price, stock or a customer rating: the catalog has none of these (web.search does).
findings.fix: Keep the when-to-call line and parameter descriptions and move the loosening and dataset narrative out of the description.

findings.title: Catalog product default top_k does not match the three-product display
findings.problem: top_k defaults to 5 while the reply shows at most three products, and the schema gives no guidance on choosing it, so the model may request and process more results than needed.
findings.fix: State in the description that the default should be three unless the answer needs more candidates for reconciliation.

context_engineering.summary: The context is well grounded and well fenced, but it is verbose, repeats catalog and loosening rules across files, and has a budget-loosening conflict and a few missing controls (catalog recall checks, shopper-message fence) that should be fixed.
